ttp-attack-mapping-reliability.rationale: HELD AT 3, evidence base unchanged since the cycle-10 assessment (cycle 11 was a selection-only T5 and cycle 12 touched only institutional-incident-real-world-impact), so this is a re-affirmation and NOT a re-litigation. One-line justification: the primary candidate is supported by src-0002 (CTIBench CTI-ATE F1=0.6388 for GPT-4-turbo vs ~71-72% on knowledge-recall CTI-MCQ/CTI-RCM) and src-0005 (CyberSOCEval; test-time-scaling gains do not transfer to cybersecurity reasoning, benchmarks 'far from saturating'), which is two independent sources on the primary candidate = level 3. THE CYCLE-10 FINDING THAT STILL HAS NOT BEEN ACTIONED, restated because it is the only thing standing between this issue and a 4: src-0007 (CyberThreat-Eval, Mar 2026) is a third independent measurement of the same sub-task on real production CTI material -- ATT&CK TTP identification precision/recall 0.2787/0.2270 (GPT-4o), 0.3480/0.1759 (o3-mini), 0.2387/0.1846 (GPT-4o FT), 0.1771/0.1414 (GPT-4o-mini FT) -- and it bears directly on open_question[0] (2026-era models are still nowhere near solving the task) and open_question[2] (fine-tuned GPT-4o scores BELOW zero-shot GPT-4o, so ATT&CK-specific fine-tuning points the wrong way, echoing src-0001). But the graph's candidate_resolution still lists evidence [src-0002, src-0005] and no T2/T3 has attached src-0007 in four cycles, so the STATE does not record a three-source claim and T4 cannot create one by asserting it in a rationale. src-0007 is listed in this entry's evidence array as T4's read of what bears on the issue, not as a substitute for the graph edit. Still not 4 for the reason given at cycle 10 and unchanged since: open_question[1] (human-analyst baseline F1 for ATT&CK technique extraction) is wholly unaddressed, so we cannot say whether 0.64 is near or far from human performance -- that is the counterargument that matters most for level 4, and level 4 requires counterarguments addressed, not merely listed. Secondary weakness: src-0005's per-model numeric scores were never captured and cycle 9's G2 pass confirmed its claims in substance but explicitly NOT verbatim, so one of the two attached sources is the weakest-verified in the base. No open contradiction on this issue, so no g3 demotion applies.

ioc-extraction-reliability.rationale: HELD AT 2, evidence unchanged since cycle 10. One-line justification: three candidate_resolutions of which candidate 1 (LANCE 97.6% F1) rests on src-0003 ALONE and candidate 2 (vanilla-LLM precision 0.8240 GPT-4o / 0.8503 o3-mini / 0.8846 GPT-4o-FT / 0.6944 GPT-4o-mini-FT over 1310 expert-annotated IoCs) rests on src-0007 ALONE, with the only multi-source candidate (candidate 3, the scaffolding-not-the-model synthesis, src-0003 + src-0007 + src-0008) deliberately held at status 'proposed' because no source tests it -- two single-source candidates plus one proposed synthesis is the textbook shape of a level 2. The rubric's bar for 3 is that the PRIMARY CANDIDATE be supported by >=2 independent sources, not that the issue accumulate 2 sources; src-0003 and src-0007 do not jointly support one claim, they pull in opposite directions on magnitude, which is why ctr-0001 exists. G3 GATE ARITHMETIC, stated separately so it is auditable: pre-demotion score on the merits = 2; ctr-0001 is open against this issue; I applied the CEILING reading (score may not exceed scale_max - g3_contradiction_demotion = 3), so the gate is NOT binding here and post-demotion = 2. WHICH READING AND WHY, for the fourth cycle running: prompts/t4_assess.md step 3 specifies a SUBTRACTION (lose 2 points, floor 0) while scripts/validate_state.py lines 144-156 implements a CEILING, and the two specifications genuinely disagree. I applied the ceiling for consistency with cycles 10 and 11 and for the substantive reason cycle 10 gave: the rubric's levels are definitions of states (0 = 'no candidate resolutions', 1 = 'no supported resolution') and this issue has three candidate_resolutions of which two are supported, so subtracting to 0 would attach a label that is factually false of the issue and would corrupt the weakest-link selector that reads these numbers. The ceiling achieves what the gate is for -- an unresolved conflict blocks the top of the scale -- without corrupting the bottom of it. The discrepancy is real and unresolved; T4 has no standing to reconcile it by editing either file, and it is carried forward (item [4]). Note that the two readings select different issues downstream: under subtraction this issue would be the graph's unique weakest link at 0-1 and would monopolise T5; under the ceiling it sits at 2 tied with consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode, with an attempt penalty against it (attempts [9], within the last 5 cycles of 13). ctr-0001's three confounds (SYSTEM: LANCE is regex+LLM+human-validation vs src-0007's Table 4 headed 'Vanilla LLMs'; METRIC: 97.6% F1 vs precision-only with no recall reported; CORPUS: 50 public threat reports vs an unnamed company's internal workflow) remain unresolved, and its stated resolution path (recover recall/F1 from src-0007's released code, or find a head-to-head) has not been attempted.

consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode.rationale: HELD AT 2, evidence unchanged since cycle 10. One-line justification: BOTH candidate_resolutions cite evidence [src-0001] and nothing else, so however well verified that source is, this is single-source support and single-source support is a 2 by definition of the rubric. The verification quality is genuinely high -- cycle 7's G2 pass re-fetched https://arxiv.org/html/2503.23175v1 and re-confirmed the model identities (gpt4o, gemini-1.5-pro-latest, mistral-large-2), the 350-report set, the 10-re-prompt bootstrapped-CI method (max CI width 0.02 extraction vs 0.06 generation) and all ten Table-6 gpt4o ECE/Brier values -- and that is exactly the point: high confidence in ONE source is still one source. The second candidate sharpens the first using the same source, so two candidates are not two sources. Corroboration was searched for and rejected twice: src-0007 reports precision/recall only with no repeated-query consistency measure and no ECE/Brier anywhere, and src-0008 measures a code-analysis task rather than CTI reasoning. Cycle 12 added four sources (src-0009, src-0010, src-0011, src-0012) and none of them touch consistency or calibration at all -- they are two institutional publication pages, a citation-validity audit and an incident report -- so nothing has changed here either. Still logged as an unattached lead rather than a second source: src-0008's Tables 6-7 show Cohere emitting 625 'Don't Know' responses and Gemini emitting 0, with Gemini also carrying by far the highest hallucination rate (4.8% vs Anthropic 0.11%, ChatGPT 0.23%, Grok 0%, Cohere 0%) -- a model that never abstains being the model that most often invents an indicator is adjacent to the overconfidence phenomenon this issue is about, but it is measured on JavaScript source code, is attached to no candidate_resolution, and one cross-model correlation on n=5 vendors is not a mechanism. All four open_questions remain unaddressed. No open contradiction, so no g3 demotion. NOTE FOR THE SELECTOR: this issue is tied at the bottom with ioc-extraction-reliability but its last attempt was cycle 3 (ten cycles ago, outside the 5-cycle attempt-penalty window), whereas ioc's was cycle 9, so on the configured tie-break this is the weaker of the two.

attribution-confident-wrong-gap.rationale: HELD AT 3. One-line justification: the primary candidate rests on two genuinely independent sources, both attached -- src-0002 (CTIBench CTI-TAA over 50 real reports; GPT-4-turbo 86% plausible vs 52% correct, Gemini-1.5 74% vs 38%) and src-0004 (Heise/Der Spiegel on ENISA's APT29/'Midnight Blizzard' misattribution published in production) -- an academic benchmark plus investigative reporting on a production incident, which is the real independence that distinguishes this issue from the single-source 2s. CHECKED AGAINST CYCLE 12'S FOUR NEW SOURCES, WHICH IS THE ONLY THING THAT COULD HAVE MOVED IT, AND THEY DO NOT: src-0009 and src-0010 are ENISA's own publication pages for the two affected reports and they corroborate the incident's STRUCTURE (two reports, 1 Oct 2025 and 6 Nov 2025, both revised 09 January 2026 for link defects) but say nothing whatever about the APT29 naming error, about attribution, or about AI -- so they strengthen institutional-incident-real-world-impact without adding a third leg here. src-0012 (EY Canada) is fabricated citations in a loyalty-fraud report with no threat-actor attribution content, and src-0011 (GhostCite) audits academic citation validity. So this issue's evidence is materially unchanged and 3 stands. NOT RAISED TO 4, unchanged reason and now in its seventh cycle of being merely listed: open_question[2] -- whether src-0004's naming-convention hallucination is the same phenomenon as src-0002's quantified plausible-vs-correct gap, or a distinct citation/naming-fabrication sub-type -- is the explicit alternative explanation for the pair, and it has never been argued either way. Level 4 requires counterarguments explicitly addressed, not merely articulated. A mild new consideration recorded but NOT scored down on: cycle 12 established that ENISA's own record attributes no cause at all to the link defects, so the AI-causation of the ENISA leg still rests entirely on Der Spiegel via Heise, and spiegel.de is unreachable to this agent (carry-forward [13]). That was already true when this issue was scored 3 at cycles 7 and 10 and is not new negative evidence, so it changes no number; it does mean the second leg cannot strengthen further without a source we currently cannot reach. No open contradiction, so no g3 demotion.

task-dependent-reliability-framing.rationale: HELD AT 3, evidence unchanged since cycle 10. One-line justification: the issue's title and its own open_questions scope it to a SPECIFIC ordinal axis ('mechanical extraction < classification < attribution < generation'), and a single score is being forced to average a narrow claim that is now near-4 with an axis that is actively disputed and scores 1-2, so 3 is the stingy resultant. The narrow claim -- that CTI reliability varies sharply by sub-task rather than being one uniform property -- has a roughly four-source footing (src-0001, src-0002, src-0006, and src-0007's within-study Table 4 contrast of IoC extraction precision 0.82-0.88 against TTP identification 0.2787/0.2270 for the same models on the same corpus) and is about as well-evidenced as anything in this graph. The ordinal axis is NOT: src-0007's Table 4 cuts in its favour (extraction cleanly beats mapping in one controlled setting) while src-0006's Table 5 cuts against it by marking failure subtypes as spanning all four pipeline stages (e.g. 'Co-mention bias (Type 1.1) -- stages 1234', re-confirmed live by cycle 8's G2 pass). No contradiction entry was opened for that tension and none should be: src-0006's claim is about where failure MECHANISMS occur and src-0007's is about where performance LEVELS differ, and the same mechanism can operate at every stage while its impact is far larger on mapping than on extraction. Cycle 12's four new sources are all about institutional publication incidents and citation validity and bear on this issue not at all. THIS IS THE SIXTH CONSECUTIVE ASSESSMENT (cycles 7, 8, 9, 10, and now 13 -- 11 and 12 were not assessments) RECORDING THAT SPLITTING THIS ISSUE INTO 'task-dependence exists' and 'the specific ordinal axis' is the single highest-value structural change available to the graph, because it is the only thing that would let either half be scored honestly instead of averaged into a number that describes neither. T4 has no standing to restructure the graph; only a T2 does. No open contradiction, so no g3 demotion.

institutional-incident-real-world-impact.rationale: RAISED 2 -> 3, and this is the only score that moves this cycle. It moves because the evidence moved: cycle 12 was the first T1/T3 ever to target this issue in twelve cycles and it took the base from one secondary source to five sources across three independent origins. THE CAP THAT SET THE OLD SCORE IS GONE: cycle 10's rationale said in terms that 'single-source support caps this at 2 regardless of how well verified that source is', and that is simply no longer the situation. The existence claim is now carried by candidate 2 with evidence [src-0009, src-0010, src-0004] -- ENISA's OWN publication pages carrying verbatim revision notices ('Revision Notice - Version 1.2. (09 January 2026): This publication has been updated to edit some links.' against a 1 Oct 2025 publication date; 'Revision Notice - Version 1.2 (09 January 2026): This publication has been updated to correct some broken links and typos.' against 6 Nov 2025) -- primary institutional artefacts corroborating report count, dates, defect type and correction date, independent of the Der Spiegel/Heise chain that was previously the whole basis. And by candidate 3 with evidence [src-0012, src-0004]: a second named incident at a different institution type (EY Canada, 'Points of Attack: Uncovering Cyber Threats and Fraud in Loyalty Systems', 16 of 27 references hallucinated per GPTZero 14 May 2026, report withdrawn), discovered by the identical route of an outside party clicking through footnotes. Two incidents at two institutions via two mutually independent investigations, plus the affected institution's own correction record, clears the rubric's level-3 bar of a primary candidate supported by >=2 independent sources. The second half of the issue title also produced a real finding for the first time (candidate 4): institutional responses DIVERGED -- EY withdrew the report and invoked an 'organisation-wide commitment to the responsible use of AI', ENISA retained both reports, patched links, told the press 'human errors' while confirming AI was permitted for 'minor editorial revisions', and as of 2026-07-29 carries no AI disclosure on either page. NOT RAISED TO 4, AND THIS IS THE SCORING TRAP OF THIS CYCLE, NAMED SO NO LATER CYCLE WALKS INTO IT. (a) THE BASE RATE IS UNMEASURED AND IS BLOCKED BY SCOPE, NOT BY EVIDENCE VOLUME. Two named incidents are two data points, not a rate, and open_question[0] asks for a rate across CTI publishers. src-0011 (GhostCite) is NOT that rate and its own candidate_resolution is correctly marked 'proposed': it audits peer-reviewed conference papers (which have reviewers; CTI reports have none), defines a ghost citation as one absent from any major academic database (largely inapplicable to CTI footnotes, which are news and vendor URLs), reports per-PAPER rates (1.01% of Security-venue papers containing at least one invalid citation) that are not comparable with src-0004's per-FOOTNOTE 26/492, and its own authors call it 'a conservative lower bound'. Treating a second anecdote plus an adjacent-population audit as a resolved base rate would be the single most likely error available this cycle, and it is not being made. (b) THE AI-CAUSATION LEG IS THE WEAKEST PART OF THE ISSUE AND IT IS THE PART THE TOPIC IS ABOUT. For ENISA, AI attribution rests entirely on Der Spiegel via Heise (src-0004); ENISA's own pages assign no cause at all, and spiegel.de is unreachable to this agent (carry-forward [13]). The 26-of-492 figure remains independently unverified -- every outlet repeating it (cybernews, Tagesspiegel, derStandard) cites Der Spiegel, which is repetition, not corroboration. For EY, the '72% AI' figure is the output of GPTZero's own commercial AI-detection product; the load-bearing figure is the manually-checkable citation count, not the detector score. So what is robustly established is that FABRICATED CITATIONS reached production at two named institutions; that AI CAUSED them is well-supported for EY and reported-but-not-primary for ENISA. (c) Three of five open_questions are wholly or mostly open, and candidate 4 itself honestly concludes 'there is no single institutional response pattern to report' -- an accurate non-answer on n=2, not a resolution. Level 4 requires counterarguments addressed; these are engaged (cycle 12 engaged them carefully and this cycle engaged one further) but not settled. NO G3 DEMOTION: no contradiction is open against this issue, and cycle 12's reasoning for not opening one over ENISA's silence is endorsed rather than re-argued -- the revision notices assign no cause at all, and silence is not a competing claim, so G3's 'two supported claims in conflict' is not met. CYCLE 13 G2 RESULT FOLDED IN: this cycle re-verified src-0012's load-bearing 16-of-27 figure (see logs/cycle-013.md) and it PASSED, with the GPTZero primary's contradictory '0 of 27 references hallucinated' scorecard now demonstrably a rendering artefact rather than a competing claim, because the same page's own body text reads 'We chased down every citation. Most were hallucinated.' and 'Almost all of the URLs are broken or fake, and more than half of the titles don't correspond to real sources' and individually labels eight enumerated references 'Hallucinated'. That removes a live doubt about src-0012 but does not raise the score, because the doubt it removes was about whether the second incident is real, and the score is limited by base rate and AI-causation, not by that.
